Uragāṇām astrāṇi : nt. pl.: Missiles special to the mythical serpents.

Arjuna was to learn these missiles after reaching Indra's residence 3. 164. 29-30.

p. 9

from below after users add: Arjuna learnt it (not named) from Śakra (Indra) 3. 161. 28; 3. 164. 30 (pl. madgatāni ca yānīha sarvāstrāṇi); from Devarāja (Indra) 12. 5. 13-14;

p. 9

after 38; add: according to Bhīṣma, Arjuna's arsenal (astragrāmaḥ) included divine missiles of Mahendra (Indra), Rudra, Kubera, Yama and Varuṇa 5. 166. 32-33;

p. 9

after 7. 132. 31, 32; add: used by him also against Arjuna 7. 163. 28;

p. 9

(from below) after 4. 58. 8-9; add: on the same occasion, Bhīṣma and Arjuna used it against each other 4. 59. 21;

p. 9

(from below) after 127. add: [See Paurandara ]

Uraśā : f.: Name of a city.

Arjuna in his expedition to the north defeated Rocamāna living at Uraśā in the north-west (uraśāvāsinaṁ caiva rocamānaṁ raṇe 'jayat) 2. 24. 18.

Uraga : m. pl.): Name of a Janapada ?

Listed by Saṁjaya among the (northern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (ata ūrdhvaṁ janapadān nibodha gadato mama) 6. 10. 37, 5; also called the Deśas (deśāḥ saṁkīrtitāḥ) 6. 10. 68; (vātajāmarathoragāḥ) 6. 10. 53 (or, do we read vātajāmarathoragāḥ ?)
